collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The hardest-working families got the smallest shares: look at how food is shared, or help quietly.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has noticed that the families who did most of the harvest work got the smallest shares, while families close to the elders got more. Meanwhile, (friend)'s family cannot even give its usual share to the village store this year. What should the village do?

choices.label: Look at How Food Is Shared

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The gathering looks at how shares are decided. It is uncomfortable: some families have been getting more for years. New rules are made: shares by work and by need. (friend)'s family is excused from the store this year.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) quietly gives part of (subject.his/her) own share to (friend)'s family. The unequal sharing goes on. (subject) brings it up at every gathering. It takes a year to change.
